item.title: Trump's mediators offer Hamas formal proposal to give up its weapons in Gaza
item.summary: NPR has learned that mediators have quietly given Hamas a proposal to hand over all its weapons to ensure Gaza's reconstruction.

item.title: Fear, defiance, and anger: Iranians describe life under bombardment
item.summary: In messages to NPR, Tehran residents describe largely deserted streets roamed by paramilitary officials and vigilantes. They say security forces are banning gatherings for Nowruz, the Persian new year, this week.

item.title: As Pakistan and Afghanistan declare truce, civilians in Kabul count the cost of war
item.summary: At the Emergency Hospital, dozens crowded around a thick book to check the names of the victims killed in an airstrike on a rehabilitation center. The U.N. says over a hundred people were killed.

item.title: Sen. Blumenthal discusses reforming DHS and his concerns about the war in Iran
item.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a panelist in Sen. Markwayne Mullin's Department of Homeland Security confirmation hearing, discusses the reforms he wants for the agency and shares his views on the Iran war with NPR's Steve Inskeep.

item.title: Japan's prime minister visits the White House under shadow of Iran war
item.summary: Japan Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will be the first U.S. ally to visit the White House since President Trump asked for help in sending ships to patrol the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: The SAVE Act faces long odds in the Senate. GOP-led states are picking up the cause
item.summary: Several Republican-led states are passing their own versions of the SAVE America Act, Trump-backed legislation that would introduce new proof-of-citizenship requirements to register to vote.

item.title: Afroman prevails in cops' music video defamation suit after a brief but viral trial
item.summary: The "Because I Got High" rapper made waves in 2023 with the album and song "Lemon Pound Cake," using home video to mock a police raid on his Ohio home. The deputies lost their civil suit against him.

item.title: Singer Jill Scott is doing what she wants: 'Everything has led me to this place'
item.summary: The Grammy-winning singer describes herself as a "53-year-old woman who is maneuvering her career the way she wants to, how she wants to." Scott's new album is To Whom This May Concern.

item.title: Harry Styles' new album is a massive chart success
item.summary: This week, the biggest chart news revolves around Harry Styles all the time. Other artists, occasionally.

item.title: 'Movement never lies': 100 years of the Martha Graham Dance Company
item.summary: Graham was a creative force in the performing arts. She wanted dance to express authentic, human emotions — a revolutionary idea in the late 1920s.
